newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FORECAST - Comalco H1 seen hit by expansion.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Comalco H1 seen hit by expansion.

text.p: Aluminium company Comalco Ltd should post a weaker half-year profit next Monday due to higher interest charges tied to a smelter expansion, share analysts said this week.

Analysts predict Comalco, Australia's biggest producer of aluminium, will report on average a joint venture pre-abnormal net profit of about A$37 million in the six months ended June 30, 1997, compared with A$44 million a year ago.
Comalco, owned 67 percent by Rio Tinto, recorded joint venture pre-abnormal net earnings of just A$32.9 million in calendar 1996, compared with A$264.8 million in 1995.

The company's 1996 result was hit by lower aluminium prices, a higher Australian dollar and cost blow-outs associated with the upgrade of its Tiwai Point smelter in New Zealand and the re-start of idle capacity at its Bell Bay smelter in Tasmania.
Chris Bain, resources analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, forecasts first-half earnings of A$32 million for Comalco.
Bain said gains from higher production should be offset by higher interest costs associated with the funding of the A$1 billion expansion of its Boyne Island smelter in Queensland state.
"Their debt should be significantly higher. I expect they made steady drawdowns in the first half for the Boyne Island expansion," he said.
Bain said he expected Comalco's interest expenses would rise to about A$44 million in the first-half, compared with A$18.4 million in the same six months of 1996.
But Bain said Comalco could decide to capitalise some of the interest costs which he estimated could boost its bottom line earnings for the half by between A$5 million to A$8 million.
Comalco has a 59.75 percent interest in the expansion, which will create a third pot line at the plant and lift its output to 490,000 tonnes per year by the third quarter of 1997.
Last month Comalco said its primary aluminium production rose to 254,737 tonnes in the six months to June 30, compared with 225,477 tonnes in the previous corresponding period.
The company said the higher output was due to new cells coming on line as part of the startup of the third pot line at Boyne Island and the upgrade of the Tiwai Point smelter.
HSBC James Capel resources analyst Umit Safak forecasts Comalco's first-half profit at A$41 million.
Safak said he expected to see significant cost improvements from the company's Bell Bay and Tiwai Point smelters.
The three-month price of aluminium averaged 72.1 U.S. cents per pound on the London Metal Exchange (LME) during the first six months of 1997 compared with 72.8 cents a year earlier.
The Australian dollar averaged 77.5 U.S. cents for the half compared with 77.3 cents for the first half of 1996.
For every one U.S. cent rise in the price of aluminium, Comalco's net profit increases by about A$9 million, the company estimates.
For every one U.S. cent decline in the value of the Australian dollar, net profit rises by A$7 million.
Comalco shares stood at A$6.60 in afternoon trading on Monday, down 15 cents on Friday's close.
-- Melbourne Bureau 61-3 9286-1435
